name: The Flint household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: flint_a_w

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 January 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-01-28, 27 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-01-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1834-01-01 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

basis.note: data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json#arrival_and_origin.tables.arrival_year_of_the_known_layer, restricted to years at or before 1834.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

This states the draws that were operating in that season and chooses among them nowhere. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

persons.name: A. W. Flint

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: GRADED BY THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER — rule G2e, applied 2026-09-04. This identity is inferred because that rung fired on the civic and press rows recorded on this card, which the resident-research corpus does not read. This programme's letter-list rule of 2026-09-02 would call it a projected resident on the absence of a research row; it is superseded here, and a no-find in one corpus is not a finding about another (T-0822). KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print '‘A. W. Flint' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 28 January 1834, column 1 — dated 1834-01-28. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.summary: No reliable record in the reviewed repository corpus, exact/variant searches, 1839/1843 Chicago directories, and targeted regional/local histories could be tied to this person by more than the recorded postal name. This is a documented no-corroboration result, not evidence that the person did not exist.

sex_basis.note: A DRAW, NOT A READING. Nothing about this person says which sex they were: T-1303 refused the name and was right to. This value is drawn from the measured male share of the roll the person was named on, seeded by their own id so the draw reproduces - retype 'flint_a_w:sex_ratio' and the same face comes up. It carries no weight as evidence about this person and it is never promoted. The rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 40 under 50', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('flint_a_w:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

old_settler_deaths.the_header_admission:
Names, places * , dates, and ages at death
of some of Chicago's Old Settlers, prior to 1843, and other well - known citizens who arrived after 1843, together
with others prominently connected with Illinois history:
old_settler_deaths.note: LATER EVIDENCE OF A DEATH, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints an obituary list of old settlers, and one of its entries meets somebody of this name. THE HEADER OF THE LIST IS QUOTED ABOVE, and it is the limit the whole reading turns on. It does not mean the person was in Chicago in 1835, and it does not mean they arrived before 1843 — the list's own header, quoted above, says it also names citizens who arrived later and others merely 'prominently connected with Illinois history'. A match means one thing: a name in the 1835 layer and a name in this list agree on surname and first initial, and the list gives that name a death date and an age. The date and the interval are the payload. Whatever is carried is carried as evidence of a DEATH and of an interval the birth falls in, never as an 1835 fact and never as a grade. T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply; this file changes no record. THE AGREEMENT HERE IS A SURNAME AND ONE INITIAL: one of the two sides prints an initial where the forename would be, so a single letter is the whole of the discriminator and the match is as thin as the rule allows. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. A death notice printed in 1896 says a person of this name died on a day; under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that is later evidence about a DEATH, and it is never an 1835 residence. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

people.matched_by: Surname 'Flint' folds to the same string as the entry's, and the given name of both begins A.
people.birth_year_arithmetic: The page prints the death as 'March 13, 1886' and the age as 'aged 73½'. An age of 73 years and 6 months means at least that and less than 73 years and 7 months, so the birth falls between 1812-08-14 and 1812-09-13: the birth year is 1812. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth.
people.as_read: Flint, Dr. Austin, died, New York City, March 13, 1886, aged 73½.
